A proven Fourier/Parseval comparison bounds average squared circular norm increments; Haar rotational invariance and the conditional covariance of the projected tangent direction give exact derivative energy (n-d)/(n(n-1)), so the universal constant is (d-1)/(n-1). Dominated convergence at coalescing unit vectors proves sharpness. Rank-one angular integration yields the exact positive-probability and expected-improvement functions and their asymptotics. n=2, d=1, d=n and antipodal vectors are covered. The standalone independent finite computational repetitions support but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The exact sharp dimension-dependent fraction answers a natural open constant-estimation question for a recently proposed random-section Frank-Wolfe oracle, improving its quantitative expected-oracle guarantees and optimally extending them to two-dimensional sections. The proved boundary between d=1 (vanishing relative gain near an optimum) and d>=2 (positive uniform gain) is structurally relevant to choosing sketch dimension. The explicit one-line success probability and gap^(3/2) law quantify a substantive failure mechanism even on the simplest smooth strongly convex body, rather than an arbitrary numerical variant.
